page: Microsoft Azure D16pds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DPDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an ARM64 architecture powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. The server is equipped with 16 dedicated physical cores operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz, with one thread per core. Memory capacity is 64.0 GB, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 614 GB local disk that is Premium Storage capable. There are no GPUs present on this instance.

Benchmark results place the D16pds_v5 primarily in the average performance tier, though some single-core and specialized tasks show weaker relative performance. The server achieves average scores in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, alongside average memory bandwidth performance, reaching 1125.92 GB/sec for small block cached reads and 129.87 GB/sec for large block uncached reads. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the bottom 25%. Similarly, LLM prompt processing speeds are weak, registering 340.95 tokens/sec for a small model and 19.12 tokens/sec for a medium model, whereas text generation speeds remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture provides a resource-dense hardware profile with dedicated physical cores, offering a favorable balance of compute and memory resources without hyperthreading overhead. Given the average performance in database operations and static web serving throughput, this server is appropriate for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, web serving, and database operations that benefit from local storage, while being less optimal for single-threaded compute-bound tasks or heavy cryptographic operations.
description: Microsoft Azure D16pds_v5 is an ARM64-based virtual machine from the DPDSv5 family, utilizing a 16-core Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It features 64.0 GB of RAM, a 614 GB local disk, and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 28887.7 and a PassMark database operations score of 11285.91. However, single-core performance represents a tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the bottom 25%. The instance offers qualitative cost efficiency through dedicated physical cores and a balanced resource profile. It is suitable for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving, but less effective for single-threaded or prompt-processing tasks.
